# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

The Paigasus AI SDK (codename **Helikon**, after Mt Helicon where Pegasus's hoof struck the Hippocrene spring). A Rust SDK for building AI agents. All crates live under the `paigasus-helikon-*` namespace.

The full architectural reference lives in Notion: ["Crate Reference"](https://www.notion.so/355830e8fbaa813c92e8c1aa9985fd3f). Linear project: `Paigasus Helikon` (issues prefixed `SMA-`).

## Common commands

```bash
cargo build --workspace                              # all 14 crates
cargo build --workspace --all-features               # facade with every optional crate
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin helikon
cargo run -p paigasus-helikon-cli --bin paigasus-helikon
```

To reproduce **every** CI gate locally (matches `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job-for-job):

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-features
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --all-features --no-deps
DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD=80 NIGHTLY_CHANNEL=nightly-2026-05-01 \
  bash scripts/check-doc-coverage.sh                 # requires: rustup toolchain install nightly-2026-05-01
npm ci                                               # once, or after package-lock.json changes
npx markdownlint-cli2                                # reads .markdownlint-cli2.jsonc
bash scripts/check-markdownlint-config.sh            # asserts that config is in force
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh         # cargo-visible workflow env is uniform
bash scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync-selftest.sh # …and its parser still parses (fmt runs both)
bash scripts/check-release-gaps-selftest.sh            # release gap report + release-plz.yml guards (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade-selftest.sh      # the cascade guard keeps its rule (fmt runs it)
bash scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh                 # breaking bump needs breaking dependents (PR only; fmt runs it)
```

The full list lives in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (single source of truth for contributor policies).

## Workspace layout

15 crates under `crates/`. The facade `paigasus-helikon` re-exports `paigasus-helikon-core` unconditionally and the other 12 sibling crates behind Cargo features.

Every crate carries a real implementation and publishes to crates.io; zero name-claim stubs remain (first published in SMA-385, last ascends in SMA-333). One standing exception: `paigasus-helikon-cli` publishes as a **binary** crate — its lib target is internal (`missing_docs` opted out), carries no stability guarantee, and exists only so `cargo install paigasus-helikon-cli` resolves. `paigasus-helikon-sessions-testkit` publishes as a normal library crate (SMA-805); the three session backends keep a path-only dev-dependency on it. Exact versions move every release — read each crate's `Cargo.toml`, don't trust numbers written here.

Workspace inheritance is **mandatory**: per-crate `Cargo.toml`s only set `name`, `description`, and any crate-specific bits. Everything else (`edition`, `rust-version`, `authors`, `license`, `repository`, `homepage`, `keywords`, `categories`) inherits from `[workspace.package]` in the root `Cargo.toml`. Don't hardcode these per-crate.

**Per-crate version is the one exception.** No stubs remain, so the 4-step ascend recipe is now historical — but two caveats still bite any PR that hand-bumps a version:

- **If a crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too**, along with its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and CHANGELOG. `cargo publish --verify` builds the tarball against the **registry** core, so otherwise the publish fails and release-plz deadlocks.
- **Any PR that hand-bumps a sibling must ALSO bump the facade** (`crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` version + its self-pin + CHANGELOG). release-plz does not bump the facade for a sibling version that is already at target when the PR merges, so a manual bump silently leaves the facade advertising stale dep reqs. (`dependencies_update = true` only makes the release PR run `cargo update` on `Cargo.lock`; it does not cascade version bumps.)
- **A breaking bump of a crate needs a breaking bump of each crate that depends on it.** release-plz gives a dependent without its own commits only a patch bump (release-plz#1599), and users then get two copies of the crate. The `fmt` job runs `scripts/check-breaking-cascade.sh` to enforce this. See `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md` → "A breaking change in a crate with dependents".
- Feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.

Full lifecycle, the 4-step recipe, and the SMA-321/SMA-346 postmortems: `docs/runbooks/release-ascend.md`.

Third-party version pins live in `[workspace.dependencies]` (root). Members reference them via `dep.workspace = true`. Internal crate paths are also in `[workspace.dependencies]` so the facade can use `workspace = true` consistently.

## Non-obvious patterns to preserve

- **Feature naming**: kebab-case in `[features]` (`runtime-tokio`), snake-case in `pub use` aliases (`runtime_tokio`). They must stay paired across the facade's `Cargo.toml` and `src/lib.rs`.
- **`paigasus-helikon-cli` uses `autobins = false`** because the `paigasus-helikon` (hyphen) binary maps to `src/bin/paigasus_helikon.rs` (underscore — hyphens are illegal in Rust filenames). Removing `autobins = false` reintroduces a phantom `paigasus_helikon` binary that conflicts with the explicit `[[bin]]` entry.
- **`paigasus-helikon-macros` is a proc-macro crate from day one** (`[lib] proc-macro = true`). Don't convert it to a regular lib even though it currently has no macros.
- **The `paigasus-helikon` facade lib shares its name with the `paigasus-helikon` CLI binary by design** (Notion ref's "fully-qualified shim alias"). This produces a non-fatal `cargo doc` filename-collision warning. Don't "fix" it by renaming either — both names are user-facing API. The accepted future fix is `doc = false` on the CLI binary entry.
- **License is dual `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`** (decided 2026-05-20, reversing the 2026-05-16 MIT-only call). Both `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` live at the repo root; the workspace metadata is `license = "Apache-2.0 OR MIT"`. Per Rust ecosystem convention — no Apache-only or MIT-only crates in the workspace. Contributions are accepted under the same dual license by default (the standard inbound-equals-outbound clause is restated in `README.md`).
- **MSRV is `1.94`** (workspace-package level; raised from 1.85 in SMA-329 because sqlx 0.9.0 declares `rust-version = "1.94.0"` — the pre-existing highest floor in the workspace). If a dep raises MSRV, bump `rust-version` to what cargo demands rather than downgrading the dep.
- **Workspace-wide `missing_docs` enforcement** lives in root `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.lints.rust] missing_docs = "warn"`). Each non-CLI crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. The CLI overrides locally with `[lints.rust] missing_docs = "allow"` and does **not** include `workspace = true` — cargo treats `[lints] workspace = true` and an inline `[lints.<tool>]` table as mutually exclusive. When adding a new crate, copy the opt-in block. When adding a new `pub use` re-export to the facade, give it a `///` doc comment or `-D warnings` will fail the docs job.
- **`cargo msrv` has no `--workspace` flag.** The msrv workflow verifies one representative inheriting crate: `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify`. Because every member uses `rust-version.workspace = true`, success on one is success on all. Don't "fix" the workflow by adding `--workspace`; that's what the first SMA-305 CI run died on.
- **Nightly is date-pinned** (`NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN: nightly-2026-05-01` at the workflow `env:` level in `ci.yml`, threaded into the doc-coverage script as `NIGHTLY_CHANNEL`). The rustdoc JSON coverage format is `-Z unstable-options` and can shift between nightlies; floating `nightly` would be a CI footgun. Bumping is a one-line follow-up chore, not an emergency.
- **Bootstrap commits on release infrastructure must use `chore(...)` or `docs(...)` types**, never `feat`/`fix`. release-plz parses every commit since the last per-crate tag — a `feat(workspace): ...` commit that touches every `Cargo.toml` would attribute a bump to every crate. The SMA-307 bootstrap PR followed this rule; the same rule applies to any future `release-plz.toml` or `release-plz.yml` edits.

## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:

- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest

- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"

• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"

## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. browser-use <<'PY'

23	# be silently corrupted on a Windows checkout, the same defensive reasoning
24	# as the binary rule below.

27	# Gemini SSE fixtures (SMA-827): split on literal newlines by tests, so pin LF.

31	# otherwise rewrite every file with CRLF and diverge from the ubuntu-only CI gate.
32	# Listed BEFORE the bedrock `binary` rule below on purpose -- gitattributes is
33	# last-match-wins, so a broader `*.md` rule appended after `binary` would
34	# silently text-normalize a `.md` file dropped into that fixture tree, exactly
35	# the silent corruption the `binary` rule's own comment exists to prevent.
36	*.md text eol=lf

38	# Bedrock is the one subject with a binary wire format:
39	# `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` frames are a length-prefixed header block
40	# wrapped in two CRC-32s, so *any* eol translation corrupts them into frames the
41	# SDK's decoder rejects. This rule is listed LAST on purpose — gitattributes
42	# resolves later matches first, so no broader glob above can turn a file under
43	# this directory back into `text`.
44	#

46	# `eventstream::frame` rather than checking in opaque `.bin` blobs, so no file
47	# matches this yet. It is here so that a later fixture dropped into that
48	# directory cannot be silently corrupted on a Windows checkout — which would
49	# present as the translator dropping unknown events, not as a checkout bug.

540	- If a `finish_reason` was observed, `finish()` emits exactly one `Finish`, as
541	  the last event of the stream.
542	- **If no `finish_reason` was observed (premature EOF), no `Finish` is
543	  emitted** and the stream simply ends. Fabricating `Finish::Stop` would make a
544	  truncated generation indistinguishable from a clean completion — and because
545	  `ModelTurnAccumulator` initialises `finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop`
546	  (`core/src/model.rs:558`), the truncated text would be committed to session
547	  history as final.
548	
549	This is what makes the usage/finish ordering correct, and it is **measured, not
550	inferred** (Appendix B, P1). The tail of a real stream is:
551	
552	```
553	data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}
554	data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":6,"prompt_tokens":8,…}}
555	data: [DONE]
556	```
557	
558	The usage snapshot arrives in a **separate trailing chunk after** the chunk
559	carrying `finish_reason`. Any inline-`Finish` design therefore emits `Finish`
560	then `Usage` on **every single turn**, violating `core/src/model.rs:63` — this
561	is not an edge case. An error frame arriving after the finish chunk is likewise
562	safe, because `Finish` has not been emitted yet.
563	
564	**Cancellation** follows the OpenAI provider: `tokio::select!` with `biased` on
565	the cancel arm, at both the initial request future and each upstream poll. Per
566	`core/src/model.rs:66-68`, a cancelled stream ends **without** `Finish`.
567	
568	## 10. Error handling (`error.rs`)
569	
570	### 10.1 The error envelope, as measured
571	
572	LiteLLM returns `{"error": {"message", "type", "param", "code"}}`. The
573	first draft's classification rested on a wrong reading of two of those fields.
574	Measured on 1.97.0 (Appendix B, P7/P10/P11):
575	
576	| Provoked condition | HTTP | `code` | `type` |
577	|---|---|---|---|
578	| `litellm.InternalServerError` | 500 | `"500"` | `null` |
579	| `litellm.RateLimitError` | 429 | `"429"` | `"throttling_error"` |

- If a `finish_reason` was observed, `finish()` emits exactly one `Finish`, as
  the last event of the stream.
- **If no `finish_reason` was observed (premature EOF), no `Finish` is
  emitted** and the stream simply ends. Fabricating `Finish::Stop` would make a
  truncated generation indistinguishable from a clean completion — and because
  `ModelTurnAccumulator` initialises `finish_reason: FinishReason::Stop`
  (`core/src/model.rs:558`), the truncated text would be committed to session
  history as final.

This is what makes the usage/finish ordering correct, and it is **measured, not
inferred** (Appendix B, P1). The tail of a real stream is:

carrying `finish_reason`. Any inline-`Finish` design therefore emits `Finish`
then `Usage` on **every single turn**, violating `core/src/model.rs:63` — this
is not an edge case. An error frame arriving after the finish chunk is likewise
safe, because `Finish` has not been emitted yet.

the cancel arm, at both the initial request future and each upstream poll. Per
`core/src/model.rs:66-68`, a cancelled stream ends **without** `Finish`.

## Evidence: the defect is reachable in production

The ticket presents the fragmented shape as hypothetical. It is not.

LiteLLM **1.98.0** was run in Docker against a local fake OpenAI-compatible
upstream emitting a name split across two post-id deltas. LiteLLM passed the
fragments through **verbatim** — `{"name":"get_"}` then `{"name":"weather"}`,
with no reassembly. LiteLLM does not normalize tool-call names.

This matters for severity. LiteLLM's purpose is fronting arbitrary backends, so
the exposure is "any backend that fragments a name," not "OpenAI, which does
not." The two captures are reproduced verbatim as the fixtures in §5.

### Capture method (and why the recorded blocker does not apply)

`providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` carries this
provenance header, recorded during SMA-451:

> Provenance: HAND-AUTHORED. […] the parallel tool-call payload is hand-built
> because a keyless LiteLLM mock cannot emit streamed tool calls
> (`mock_tool_calls` is ignored on the proxy's streaming path).

That is accurate about `mock_response`/`mock_tool_calls`, and it is why this
design does **not** use them. Pointing LiteLLM at a local fake
OpenAI-compatible upstream via `api_base` sidesteps the limitation entirely:
the proxy performs its real translation over a real HTTP stream, and what it
emits is genuine LiteLLM output. No API key is involved.

Reproduction:

```yaml
# litellm_config.yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: shape-fragment
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini-fragment
      api_key: sk-fake-not-used
      api_base: http://host.docker.internal:8099/v1
```

`main-latest` is a mutable tag, so it alone does not pin what was actually
run; the capture used the image at digest
`sha256:3a1980074ff2ac13883e0ffee1bebec345d8addd004be251079cee173b0e8305`,
which at capture time resolved to LiteLLM 1.98.0. The `docker run` below
pins that digest so the reproduction is reproducible:

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name litellm -p 4000:4000 \
  -v "$PWD/litellm_config.yaml:/app/config.yaml" \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm@sha256:3a1980074ff2ac13883e0ffee1bebec345d8addd004be251079cee173b0e8305 \
  --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000
curl -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \
  -d '{"model":"shape-fragment","stream":true,
       "stream_options":{"include_usage":true},
       "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"weather in Berlin?"}],
       "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_weather",
                 "parameters":{"type":"object",
                 "properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}}}}}]}'
```

The fake upstream is ~90 lines of `http.server` returning a fixed SSE frame
list; it is a throwaway capture harness and is **not** committed. The captured
output is what the repo keeps.

### Captured frames (fragmented shape, `tool_calls` arrays only)

```json
{"id":"call_abc","function":{"arguments":"","name":"get_"},"type":"function","index":0}
{"function":{"arguments":"","name":"weather"},"type":"function","index":0}
{"function":{"arguments":"{\"city\":\"Berlin\"}"},"type":"function","index":0}
```

Two things this settles by inspection rather than assumption:

1. **LiteLLM does not reassemble the name** — `get_` and `weather` arrive as
   separate `name` fields on separate deltas, exactly as the fake upstream sent
   them.
2. **LiteLLM emits `index` on every tool-call delta**, including continuations
   that carry no `id`. So `providers-litellm` correlates these under
   `Key::Index(0)` throughout, and the `Key::Id` branch (`stream.rs:154`) is not
   reached by LiteLLM's own output. The dual-keying hazard noted in §2 is
   therefore latent rather than reachable through this proxy — which is why §2
   guards against it rather than restructuring the keying.

LiteLLM also reorders keys and adds `"type":"function"` to continuation deltas
that the upstream did not send; both are cosmetic and already tolerated by the
crate's `ToolCallChunk` deserializer.

## Decision

Of the ticket's three options, this design takes **defer the name until it can
be established as complete** (option 1). Rejected:

- *Allow fragments; make the accumulator append.* Would change the documented
  contract on `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta` **and** `AgentEvent::ToolCallDelta` —

The "stops reading at `Finish`" pattern is nonetheless real, not hypothetical,
and there is an in-repo witness: `crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:237`
does `ModelEvent::Finish { .. } => break`. It happens to ignore `Usage`
(`_ => {}`), so it is unaffected today — but it is the honest evidence that a
contract-abiding consumer written tomorrow would lose the snapshot.

## Evidence

Reproduced first-hand against a keyless LiteLLM proxy (`main-stable`,
Docker 29.6.2). Full traces in Appendix A. The essential shape:

```text
data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}     ← Finish emitted here
data: {…"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{…}}                ← Usage arrives after
data: [DONE]
```

Two details the issue does not record, both confirmed by capture:

1. The usage-bearing chunk still carries `choices: [{index:0, delta:{}}]`, and
   omits the `finish_reason` key entirely (it is absent, not `null`).
2. With `include_usage` omitted, **no trailing usage chunk appears at all** —
   the stream ends `finish_reason` chunk → `[DONE]`. This case is why the
   terminal event must be anchored to EOF.

**Provenance limit, stated up front.** This was confirmed against LiteLLM's
mock backend, **not** against `api.openai.com` — no first-party key was
available. The issue and this spec both generalise to "OpenAI"; the direct
evidence is one proxy. Two things keep that from undermining the work: the
trailing-usage split is what the OpenAI Chat Completions streaming spec
describes for `include_usage`, and the fix is strictly more permissive — it is
correct whether usage arrives on the finish chunk, on a trailing chunk, or
never. Confirming against the first-party API remains worthwhile and is noted
in the follow-ups.

- `tests/fixtures/chat_content_filter.txt:3`

implementation looks correct, so a test written from them passes on broken

257	| Multi-`finish_reason` stream | one `Finish`, last wins | Δ (was one per chunk) | removes post-`Finish` deltas |
258	
259	### Fixtures
260	
261	`tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` — **new**. The finish chunk,
262	usage chunk, and `[DONE]` are transcribed byte-for-byte from Appendix A.1; the
263	ten content deltas are reconstructed by hand in the same shape (the appendix
264	elides them). The provenance comment must say exactly that — "transcribed
265	verbatim" would overclaim.
266	
267	`chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` and `chat_content_filter.txt` — restructured so
268	`usage` sits on its own trailing chunk matching the captured envelope (empty
269	`delta`, no `finish_reason` key), with the tool-call and content-filter
270	payloads otherwise unchanged.
271	
272	`tests/chat_wire.rs:34-41` — **the third instance, and the one that states the
273	falsehood in English.** It builds an inline SSE body welding `usage` onto the
274	`finish_reason` chunk, under the comment *"Usage arrives on the same chunk as
275	`finish_reason` (per OpenAI's `stream_options.include_usage: true`
276	behaviour)"* — precisely what Appendix A refutes. Restructure the body to the
277	captured envelope and delete the comment. A spec arguing "the fixtures are the
278	entire regression signal" cannot leave the written-down false belief in place.
279	
280	**Provenance comments are SSE comment lines.** These files are fed to a real
281	SSE parser via wiremock, so each provenance note must be a `:`-prefixed line.
282	A `#` or `//` line would parse as an unknown field — harmless but silently
283	wrong, and a bad precedent for the Anthropic fixtures, whose tests do split on
284	literal `\n`.
285	
286	**Envelope caveat.** The capture is LiteLLM's mock, not `api.openai.com`. Its
287	usage chunk carries `"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}]`; OpenAI's own API
288	sends `"choices":[]` (async-openai documents the field as *"Can also be empty
289	for the last chunk if you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`"*).
290	Both parse identically — the choices loop simply does not run — but the anchor
291	fixture must not silently claim first-party provenance. Record the limitation
292	in its comment and add a second hand-authored variant with `"choices":[]` so
293	both envelopes are covered.
294	
295	**Capture limits, established empirically.** A keyless LiteLLM mock cannot
296	provoke either non-happy path:
297	
298	- `content_filter` — not reproducible on demand by any mock.
299	- `tool_calls` — `mock_tool_calls` is silently ignored on the proxy's streaming
300	  path; a request carrying `tools` with `tool_choice: "required"` still returns
301	  plain mock text (0 occurrences of `tool_calls` in the stream).
302	
303	So exactly one fixture is genuinely captured, and the other two borrow its
304	envelope. The provenance comments must say so plainly rather than imply a
305	recording that did not happen.
306	
307	**Line endings.** `.gitattributes` pins `text eol=lf` for the Anthropic fixture
308	directory and the tools fixtures, but **not** for
309	`providers-openai/tests/fixtures/`. That gap is not a live bug: the Anthropic
310	tests split fixtures on literal `\n`, whereas the OpenAI tests hand the bytes
311	to wiremock as `text/event-stream` and let a real SSE parser read them
312	(`tests/chat_streaming.rs:25-33`) — and SSE treats `\r\n` as a valid line
313	terminator. A CRLF checkout would therefore still parse, which is why Windows
314	CI is green today.
315	
316	Add the rule anyway, for the reason the tools entry already gives ("pin LF for
317	consistency with the convention above"): these are wire-format fixtures whose
318	bytes are asserted on, and a future test that does split on `\n` would
319	otherwise fail only on Windows. Stated as consistency and defence, not as a
320	fix for a present failure.
321	
322	### Tests
323	
324	Tests are labelled by what they can actually catch. Only the first is a
325	regression test in the strict sense; conflating the two categories is how the
326	original blind spot was rationalised.
327	
328	**Regression — fails on pre-fix code:**
329	
330	1. Against `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`: assert `Finish` is the final event,
331	   that a `Usage` precedes it, that there is **exactly one** `Finish`, and that
332	   the usage carries the real captured counts (`input_tokens: 8`,
333	   `output_tokens: 6`). The count assertions matter — without them a translator
334	   emitting a zeroed `Usage` would pass.
335	2. **Multi-choice / repeated `finish_reason`:** a `ChatTranslator` unit test
336	   asserting exactly one `Finish` with last-wins, using the A/B/C chunk
337	   sequence above. Fails pre-fix, which emits two.
338	
339	**New-code guards — pass both before and after; they protect the *fix* from
340	regressing, and are not evidence the bug existed:**
341	
342	3. No-usage stream (`finish_reason` → EOF) still emits exactly one `Finish`.
343	4. Truncated stream (no `finish_reason`) emits no `Finish`.
344	5. Cancellation fired **after** the finish chunk emits no `Finish`. The

435	No mdBook or README edit. `ChatTranslator` is `pub(crate)`; no public API,
436	feature flag, crate status, or documented concept changes. Recorded as a
437	conscious call per CLAUDE.md rather than a silent skip.
438	
439	## Appendix A — captured traces
440	
441	Environment: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, Docker 29.6.2, arm64 macOS,
442	`gpt-4o-mini` with `mock_response`, no API key.
443	
444	### A.1 — `stream_options.include_usage: true`
445	
446	Middle content deltas elided; the tail is verbatim.
447	
448	```text
449	data: {"id":"chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0-…","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1786898631,"model":"mock-fast","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"Hel"}}]}
450	…
451	data: {"id":"chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0-…","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1786898631,"model":"mock-fast","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"."}}]}
452	
453	data: {"id":"chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0-…","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1786898631,"model":"mock-fast","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}
454	
455	data: {"id":"chatcmpl-1cc5e8c0-…","created":1786898631,"model":"mock-fast","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":6,"prompt_tokens":8,"total_tokens":14,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0}}}
456	
457	data: [DONE]
458	```
459	
460	Note the key-order difference on the usage chunk (`created` before `object`) —
461	incidental, but preserved in the transcribed fixture since it is what the wire
462	produced.
463	
464	### A.2 — `stream_options` omitted
465	
466	```text
467	data: {…,"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{},"finish_reason":"stop"}]}
468	
469	data: [DONE]
470	```
471	
472	No trailing usage chunk. This is the case that rules out the Bedrock pattern.
473	
474	### A.3 — tool calls not provokable
475	
476	`mock-tools` configured with `mock_tool_calls`, requested with `tools` and
477	`tool_choice: "required"`: the stream returns plain mock text and contains zero
478	`tool_calls` occurrences.
479	
480	## Reproduction
481	
482	```yaml
483	model_list:
484	  - model_name: mock-fast
485	    litellm_params:
486	      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
487	      api_key: fake-key
488	      mock_response: "Hello from the mock backend."
489	general_settings: {master_key: REDACTED}
490	```
491	
492	```bash
493	docker run -d --name litellm-probe -p 4000:4000 \
494	  -v "$PWD/litellm-config.yaml:/app/config.yaml" \
495	  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000
496	
497	curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
498	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
499	  -d '{"model":"mock-fast","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],
500	       "stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}}'
501	```

551	/// with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` → `usage` → `[DONE]`, mirroring the
552	/// litellm capture's full trace. That shape was tried first and reverted: the
553	/// design spec's §6 table asserts only **7, 1** for this scenario (`S6`), not
554	/// 3/4, and `Scenario::expects_stop_reason` (`src/lib.rs`) excludes
555	/// `FragmentedToolName` from the set of scenarios that may observe a stop

557	/// `finish_reason` and flushing it as a genuine `Finish` at end-of-stream —

511	/// `Usage` on every streaming turn. It went undetected because the fixtures
512	/// in place at the time encoded a wire shape real OpenAI-compatible servers
513	/// do not send — `usage` arriving *before* `finish_reason` rather than after.
514	/// `CleanStop` below places `usage` after the `finish_reason` chunk for
515	/// exactly that reason.
516	///
517	/// # Fixture provenance
518	///
519	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a committed fixture in this
520	/// workspace, cited on the helper that builds it:
521	///
522	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`
523	///   — the SMA-522 capture: content deltas, the `finish_reason` chunk, the
524	///   trailing `usage` chunk, `[DONE]`.
525	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/chat_wire.rs`'s
526	///   `happy_path_text_completion` fixture body — grounds the explicit
527	///   `"finish_reason":null"` OpenAI sends on every non-terminal chunk, which
528	///   is exactly the shape [`OpenAiChat::encodes_stop_reason`]'s marker must
529	///   not match.
530	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt`
531	///   — the tool-call envelope: `id`/`name` arriving with empty `arguments`,
532	///   followed by args-only continuations with no `name` key.
533	/// - `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_fragmented_name.txt`
534	///   — the committed capture of a name split across two deltas that BOTH
535	///   arrive after the `id`. Per the design spec's §6 provenance note, this is
536	///   the capture `FragmentedToolName`'s shape must be drawn from — the note
537	///   requires the committed **shape**, not byte-identical values; see
538	///   "`FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes" below for exactly
539	///   what this module substitutes (the "id resolves late" variant has no
540	///   capture anywhere in the repo and is not built here).
541	///
542	/// `chat_content_filter.txt` and `chat_text_usage_trailing_empty_choices.txt`
543	/// were read but contribute no shape this module needs: this subject serves
544	/// only `Stop` and `ToolCalls` finish reasons, and the empty-`choices` usage
545	/// variant is a second encoding of the same trailing-usage envelope already
546	/// covered by `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`.
547	///
548	/// # `FragmentedToolName` deliberately never completes
549	///
550	/// The task brief's scenario table describes `FragmentedToolName` as ending
551	/// with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` → `usage` → `[DONE]`, mirroring the
552	/// litellm capture's full trace. That shape was tried first and reverted: the
553	/// design spec's §6 table asserts only **7, 1** for this scenario (`S6`), not
554	/// 3/4, and `Scenario::expects_stop_reason` (`src/lib.rs`) excludes
555	/// `FragmentedToolName` from the set of scenarios that may observe a stop
556	/// reason. Completing the stream — which the real translator does, buffering
557	/// `finish_reason` and flushing it as a genuine `Finish` at end-of-stream —
558	/// makes `encodes_stop_reason` measure `true` against an `expects_stop_reason`

560	/// even drained. So this subject's `FragmentedToolName` script draws its
561	/// event sequence and key structure from that capture's first three frames —
562	/// not a byte-identical copy: `id`/`created`/`model` are this module's fixed
563	/// constants (`RESPONSE_ID`/`MODEL_ID`) rather than the capture's literal

565	/// and the first frame omits the capture's `"role":"assistant"` key

568	/// cleanly right after those three frames — no `finish_reason`, no `usage`,

570	/// fully exercised by that prefix alone; nothing here shortens what the
571	/// scenario tests, only when its script stops.
572	///
573	/// # SMA-566's alias regression coverage lives in the crate's own unit tests
574	///

576	/// and no delta ever introduces a second `id` — the continuation frames

584	///

587	/// as a standing regression guard for the alias fix. That guard is
588	/// `two_indexes_with_one_id_merge_into_a_single_call` and its eleven siblings
589	/// in `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs`. If a
590	/// future capture ever shows a backend reusing one `id` across two indexes,
591	/// that would be the fixture to add here; none currently committed does.

1	//! Wire-format integration tests for the Chat Completions backend.
2	//!
3	//! These tests stand up a wiremock server, point an `OpenAiModel` at
4	//! `base_url(server.uri())`, and assert on the SSE bytes the provider sees.
5	//!
6	//! Wiremock serves the entire SSE fixture as one body — these tests prove
7	//! byte-level correctness of the translator, not resilience to slow chunk
8	//! delivery.
9	
10	use futures_util::StreamExt;
11	use paigasus_helikon_core::{
12	    CancellationToken, ContentPart, FinishReason, Item, Model, ModelEvent, ModelRequest,
13	};
14	use paigasus_helikon_providers_openai::OpenAiModel;
15	use wiremock::matchers::{method, path};
16	use wiremock::{Mock, MockServer, ResponseTemplate};
17	
18	fn user_msg(text: &str) -> Item {
19	    Item::UserMessage {
20	        content: vec![ContentPart::Text {
21	            text: text.to_owned(),
22	        }],
23	    }
24	}
25	
26	#[tokio::test]
27	async fn happy_path_text_completion() {
28	    let server = MockServer::start().await;
29	
30	    // SSE body: a content-delta chunk, then a finish chunk, then a SEPARATE
31	    // trailing chunk carrying usage — the shape real OpenAI-compatible
32	    // servers emit with `stream_options.include_usage: true`. Captured from
33	    // LiteLLM; see the spec's Appendix A. async-openai requires `id`,
34	    // `created`, `model`, and `object` on every chunk.
35	    let body = concat!(
36	        "data: {\"id\":\"x\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\",\"created\":1,\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",",
37	        "\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{\"content\":\"hello\"},\"finish_reason\":null}]}\n\n",
38	        "data: {\"id\":\"x\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\",\"created\":1,\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",",
39	        "\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{},\"finish_reason\":\"stop\"}]}\n\n",
40	        "data: {\"id\":\"x\",\"object\":\"chat.completion.chunk\",\"created\":1,\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",",
41	        "\"choices\":[{\"index\":0,\"delta\":{}}],",
42	        "\"usage\":{\"prompt_tokens\":3,\"completion_tokens\":1,\"total_tokens\":4}}\n\n",
43	        "data: [DONE]\n\n",
44	    );
45	
46	    Mock::given(method("POST"))
47	        .and(path("/chat/completions"))
48	        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(200).set_body_raw(body.as_bytes(), "text/event-stream"))
49	        .mount(&server)
50	        .await;
51	
52	    let model = OpenAiModel::chat("gpt-4o")
53	        .api_key("sk-test")
54	        .base_url(server.uri())
55	        .build()
56	        .unwrap();
57	
58	    let mut req = ModelRequest::new();
59	    req.messages = vec![user_msg("hi")];
60	
61	    let stream = model.invoke(req, CancellationToken::new()).await.unwrap();
62	
63	    let events: Vec<ModelEvent> = stream
64	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
65	        .await
66	        .into_iter()
67	        .map(|r| r.expect("event was Err"))
68	        .collect();
69	
70	    // First event must be the text token.
71	    assert!(
72	        matches!(events[0], ModelEvent::TokenDelta { ref text } if text == "hello"),
73	        "expected TokenDelta(\"hello\") at events[0], got {:?}",
74	        events[0]
75	    );
76	
77	    // A Usage event must be present somewhere.
78	    assert!(
79	        events.iter().any(|e| matches!(
80	            e,
81	            ModelEvent::Usage {
82	                input_tokens: 3,
83	                output_tokens: 1,
84	                ..
85	            }
86	        )),
87	        "expected a Usage {{ input_tokens: 3, output_tokens: 1 }} event, events = {events:?}"
88	    );
89	
90	    // Finish(Stop) must be the last event.
91	    assert!(
92	        matches!(
93	            events.last().unwrap(),
94	            ModelEvent::Finish {
95	                reason: FinishReason::Stop
96	            }
97	        ),
98	        "expected Finish(Stop) as last event, got {:?}",
99	        events.last()
100	    );
101	}

105	    let server = MockServer::start().await;
106

108	        r#"{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error","code":"429"}}"#;
109	    Mock::given(method("POST"))

111	        .respond_with(ResponseTemplate::new(429).set_body_string(body))
112	        .mount(&server)

118	        .build()
119	        .unwrap();

121	    let mut req = ModelRequest::new();
122	    req.messages = vec![user_msg("hi")];
123	
124	    let stream_result = model.invoke(req, CancellationToken::new()).await;
125	
126	    // The error should surface either as Err on invoke() or as the first
127	    // stream event.  Both are acceptable per the Model trait contract.
128	    match stream_result {
129	        Err(paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError::RateLimited { .. }) => {}
130	        Err(paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError::Other(_)) => {} // acceptable if mapping degrades
131	        Ok(mut s) => {
132	            let first = s
133	                .next()
134	                .await
135	                .expect("stream should yield at least one event");
136	            assert!(
137	                matches!(
138	                    first,
139	                    Err(paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError::RateLimited { .. })
140	                        | Err(paigasus_helikon_core::ModelError::Other(_))
141	                ),
142	                "expected RateLimited or Other, got {first:?}"
143	            );
144	        }
145	        Err(other) => panic!("expected RateLimited or Other, got {other:?}"),
146	    }
147	}

1565	/// The `Model::invoke` stream contract, checked against the Anthropic Messages
1566	/// API.
1567	///
1568	/// This is the provider whose truncation defect is half the reason this suite
1569	/// exists: SMA-531 (PR #200), where a stream that ended cleanly between
1570	/// `message_delta` and `message_stop` emitted `Usage` and then nothing —
1571	/// `MessageTranslator`'s buffered stop reason was never flushed, so the
1572	/// consumer got no terminal event at all. `TruncatedAfterStopReason` below
1573	/// reproduces that shape — the same event sequence, through `message_delta`'s
1574	/// `stop_reason`/`usage` values — from the fixture the SMA-531 fix itself is
1575	/// tested against; see the Fixture provenance section below for what this
1576	/// module substitutes rather than transcribes.
1577	///
1578	/// # Fixture provenance
1579	///
1580	/// Every envelope shape below is transcribed from a fixture committed in
1581	/// `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/`, cited on the
1582	/// helper or script arm that builds it:
1583	///
1584	/// - `text_only.txt` — the baseline: `message_start` (including its top-level
1585	///   `"stop_reason":null`), a text `content_block_start`, two
1586	///   `content_block_delta`s, `content_block_stop`, `message_delta`
1587	///   (`stop_reason` + `usage` in one event), `message_stop`. Grounds
1588	///   [`message_start`], [`content_block_start_text`], [`text_delta`],
1589	///   [`content_block_stop`], [`message_delta`] and [`message_stop`], and
1590	///   `CleanStop`'s full script.
1591	/// - `eof_after_message_delta.txt` — the exact SMA-531 shape and the fixture
1592	///   the crate's own `clean_eof_after_message_delta_emits_finish` regression
1593	///   test reads: `text_only.txt`'s prefix through `message_delta`, then the
1594	///   body simply ends — no `message_stop`. `TruncatedAfterStopReason` draws
1595	///   its event sequence and `message_delta`'s `stop_reason`/`usage` values
1596	///   from this fixture (via `through_stop()`, with no `message_stop`
1597	///   appended); `message_start`'s `id`/`model` and the delta text are this
1598	///   module's own constants, not the fixture's literal values (see
1599	///   [`message_start`]'s doc).
1600	/// - `eof_mid_content_block.txt` — grounds `TruncatedMidGeneration`'s
1601	///   envelope shape (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, a
1602	///   `content_block_delta`, then EOF with no `message_delta` at all). The
1603	///   delta *count* is not grounded from this file — as with every other
1604	///   subject in this module, `opening()`'s two deltas are arbitrary content
1605	///   over a grounded envelope, not a literal transcription.
1606	/// - `stream_error.txt` — grounds `ErrorMidGeneration`'s prefix envelope
1607	///   (`message_start`, `content_block_start`, one `content_block_delta`)
1608	///   *before* its own in-band `event: error` frame. See "Why `Ending::Abort`
1609	///   and not the fixtures' own `error` event" below for why that frame itself
1610	///   is not transcribed into this script.
1611	/// - `error_after_message_delta.txt` — grounds `ErrorAfterStopReason`'s
1612	///   prefix envelope: the same event-sequence shape as
1613	///   `eof_after_message_delta.txt`'s through `message_delta` (message_start,
1614	///   content_block_start, delta(s), content_block_stop, message_delta),
1615	///   though the two fixtures are not byte-identical to each other — this one
1616	///   carries a different `message_start` id and one delta where the other
1617	///   has two — again *before* its own in-band `error` frame.
1618	/// - `parallel_tool_use.txt` and `tool_use_then_continuation.txt` — the
1619	///   `tool_use` envelope: a `content_block_start` carrying the whole `id` and
1620	///   `name` together, followed by exactly one `input_json_delta` carrying the
1621	///   whole argument JSON. Grounds [`tool_use_start`], [`input_json_delta`],
1622	///   and `ToolCallCleanStop`'s script.
1623	///
1624	/// `body_cut_inside_message_stop.txt` and `thinking_then_text.txt` were read
1625	/// but contribute no shape this module needs: the former is a byte-level cut
1626	/// of `eof_after_message_delta.txt` that the SSE parser discards down to the
1627	/// same events (already covered), and this suite has no reasoning-delta
1628	/// scenario for any subject.
1629	///
1630	/// # Why `Ending::Abort` and not the fixtures' own `error` event
1631	///
1632	/// `stream_error.txt` and `error_after_message_delta.txt` both encode
1633	/// Anthropic's real error mechanism: an in-band `event: error` SSE frame,
1634	/// parsed by `AnthropicEvent::Error` and turned into `Err(ModelError::…)` by
1635	/// `stream.rs`'s `consume`. That path is already exercised directly against
1636	/// the translator by the crate's own
1637	/// `stream_error_overloaded_terminates_with_unavailable` and
1638	/// `error_after_buffered_stop_reason_emits_no_finish` tests.
1639	///
1640	/// This module instead scripts `ErrorMidGeneration` and `ErrorAfterStopReason`

### Red-first regression tests

These fail against current code. Both go in `tests/messages_streaming.rs`.

| Test | Fixture | What it catches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clean_eof_after_message_delta_emits_finish` | new — `text_only.txt` minus the `message_stop` event | **The bug.** Current code emits `[Usage, TokenDelta, TokenDelta, Usage]` and returns at `model.rs:113` with the reason still buffered — no `Finish`. This is the AC's verified-failing test |
| `body_cut_inside_message_stop_emits_finish` | new — cut **mid-line inside** the `message_stop` event | The same bug via the shape a real byte-level cut actually takes: the partial event is discarded by the SSE parser, so this is a strictly stronger red-first test than the clean-boundary one |

### Over-firing guards

These pass today **and** after the fix. They exist so a wrong fix goes red.

| Test | Fixture | Mutation it kills |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eof_mid_content_block_emits_no_finish` | new — cut after a `content_block_delta` | `finish()` returning `Finish{Stop}` unconditionally |
| `error_after_buffered_stop_reason_emits_no_finish` | new — `message_delta` with `stop_reason`, then an in-band `error` event | A fix that flushes on the error arm. The existing `stream_error.txt` **cannot** catch this: that fixture has no `message_delta` at all, so it never buffers a reason and an error-arm flush would go undetected |

Each asserts on the **whole event sequence**, not just `last()` — an assertion on
the last element alone cannot distinguish "no `Finish`" from "no events".

### Fixture byte-level requirement

`eventsource-stream` 0.2 (`Cargo.toml:28`) follows the SSE spec: an event
dispatches on a **blank line**, and pending data at EOF is discarded. Every new
fixture whose final event must reach the translator **must** end with `\n\n`.

This is a trap, not a nicety. A truncated fixture missing its terminator never
delivers `message_delta`, so `stop_reason` is never buffered, `finish()` returns
`None`, and `clean_eof_after_message_delta_emits_finish` stays **red after the
fix** — inviting an implementer to "fix" it by making `finish()` unconditional.
The existing fixtures get this right (`text_only.txt` ends `0a0a`, verified with
`xxd`) but only by convention.

`body_cut_inside_message_stop_emits_finish` is the deliberate exception: its final
partial event has *no* terminator, and that is the point.
